subject: literature
title: KS3 Literature - Animal Farm Chapter 1: Vision and Equality
description: A source-faithful KS3 revision pack on Chapter 1 of Animal Farm. It covers Old Major's vision, the idea of equality, the Seven Commandments, Orwell's characterisation, and the early Marxist context introduced in the source pages.

data.title: Events in Chapter 1
data.instruction: Put the main events of Chapter 1 in the correct order.
items: Mr Jones locks the hen-houses and stumbles to bed.
The animals gather in the barn to hear Old Major speak.
Major describes human cruelty and imagines a better future.
Major teaches the animals 'Beasts of England'.
Mr Jones is woken by the noise and fires his gun.
The frightened animals rush back to their sleeping places.

data.title: Major's Argument
data.instruction: Arrange Major's ideas in the order they build his argument.
items: He tells the animals that their lives are miserable and short.
He blames humans for living off animal labour without giving enough back.
He argues that removing man would solve hunger and overwork.
He says all animals should act as comrades and reject human habits.
He offers a hopeful dream of a future where animals are free.

data.title: Character or Idea?
data.instruction: Sort each item into the correct category.

data.title: Vision or Warning?
data.instruction: Sort each statement by whether it presents Major's hopeful vision or Orwell's later warning.
